gap: The calendar section of Rules names the rate card in prose and gives the reader no way to it, and the one route that carries that name lands them on the wrong section while the URL claims otherwise. Measured on the running product at 127.0.0.1:8083 with the shipped dist, Hebrew, signed in as a yield owner: the Rules workspace calendar tab renders one .cal-banner reading 'lekhol eiru'a kayam makhpil timkhur ha-mekhubar le-shikhvat ha-eiru'im BE-AMUD HA-TIMKHUR. ha-shikhva mufelet ka'et...' and .cal-banner-link count is 0. The banner therefore states that a live pricing layer is moving forecast revenue, names the page that controls it, and offers no control, which is the dead-end law. It also names a destination that no longer exists under that name: pricing is now the tab 'kartis ha-ta'arifim' inside the same workspace, so the sentence sends a reader looking for a page that was renamed. The cause is one gate: CalendarEvents.jsx:330 renders the button only when typeof setActiveView === 'function', RulesWorkspace.jsx passes props.setActiveView through, and workspace-router.jsx:230-241 never gives SettingsPanel a setActiveView, so the control is compiled out on every render. Wiring that prop is NOT the fix and would produce a second dead end: measured, from the calendar tab a jump to #Pricing (exactly what setActiveView('Pricing') triggers) rewrote the URL to ?rules=rate_card#Settings while .rules-tab.active stayed 'lu'akh ha-eiru'im' and the rate card never rendered, because RulesWorkspace reads the ?rules query only at mount. The whole fix is inside P5's row and is one pass: hand CalendarEvents the workspace's own open() as an onOpenRateCard callback, render the control unconditionally, name it after the tab it opens rather than 'the Pricing page', and make RulesWorkspace follow a later ?rules change instead of only the one it mounted with. Assert both in tests/test_p5_*: that the banner always renders a control, and that the section follows the query after mount. The round-2 gap is CLOSED and verified independently: on the English Today card .ledger-scope-line now computes direction ltr, the TV icon sits at x=241 against a card whose left edge is x=240, and the characters paint 'This operator's own channel is 13 reshet: 2391 breaks judged' with the colon at x=462.5 immediately right of the isolate that ends at x=462.5, so the sentence reads. The Hebrew card is unchanged and still right to left. Ranked behind the named gap, still open: the scope line prints 2391 and 6635 with no thousands separator while the same Today screen prints 8,704 and 50,386 with one; the Today card and the licence page state the same fact in two different sentences (one isolated and locale-directed, one still dir=auto with an unisolated channel name and an extra channel count), so the shared helper this round created is used by only one of its two callers; constraints_restrictions.py stores sentence_en in the notes column and ConstraintBuilder.jsx renders it verbatim; and AiringNights prints '73 min' on one night chip while its eighteen neighbours print a count of airings, so the column cannot be scanned.
